links.outcome: ChatGPT diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, specificity versus physicians on same reports
links.effect: Physicians: accuracy 0.88, sensitivity 0.99, specificity 0.81, AUC 0.92; ChatGPT direct: 0.73, 0.95, 0.58, AUC 0.72; few-shot: 0.87, 0.99, 0.73, AUC 0.83; physicians statistically superior (P=0.0008).
links.quote: Additionally, the comparison between physicians and few-shot enhanced ChatGPT showed a T-statistic of 3.42 with a P-value of 0.0008, underscoring the physicians' statistically superior performance.

links.outcome: Model diagnostic performance across radiologist reporting styles/experience levels
links.effect: Mid-level reports: accuracy 0.76, sensitivity 0.83, specificity 0.69; high-level reports: accuracy 0.80, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.69. Performance varied slightly with report author experience.
links.quote: These findings suggest that the model's performance may slightly vary depending on the radiologist's level of experience and potentially, their unique reporting style.

links.outcome: Misdiagnoses by ChatGPT when used for diagnosis of bone tumors
links.effect: 56 benign cases misdiagnosed as malignant; 23 osteosarcoma cases misdiagnosed as osteomyelitis; 8 chondrosarcoma misdiagnosed as benign lesions; 4 chordoma as spinal tuberculosis.
links.quote: In this study, 23 osteosarcoma cases were misdiagnosed as osteomyelitis by ChatGPT.

links.outcome: Errors in differential diagnosis, missed serious conditions like malignancies
links.effect: ChatGPT misdiagnosed malignant tumors as benign or infection, e.g., 23 osteosarcoma as osteomyelitis, 8 chondrosarcoma as fibrous dysplasia or aneurysmal bone cyst; 56 benign cases labelled malignant.
links.quote: Chondrosarcoma was misdiagnosed as fibrous dysplasia or aneurysmal bone cyst in 8 cases.
